name: Ectoshade
body:
Ectoshade
CR 3

This bluish, misty outline of a man is blurred and vague, though undoubtedly presents a decrepit figure contorted in fear and rage.

XP 800
CE Medium undead (incorporeal)
Init +3; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +9

DEFENSE

AC 16, touch 16, flat-footed 12 (+2 deflection, +3 Dex, +1 dodge)
hp 32 (5d8+10)
Fort +3, Ref +4, Will +7
Defensive Abilities incorporeal; Immune undead traits
Weaknesses partial incorporeality

OFFENSE

Speed fly 40 ft. (good)
Melee incorporeal touch +7 (3d6)
Special Attacks frightful scream (DC 14)

STATISTICS

Str —, Dex 17, Con —, Int 6, Wis 12, Cha 15
Base Atk +3; CMB +6; CMD 19
Feats Dodge, Iron Will, Weapon Focus (touch)
Skills Fly +15, Perception +9
Languages Common

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Frightful Scream (Su)

As a standard action, an ectoshade can let out a blood-curdling scream, increasing the fear level of every creature in a 30 ft. cone by one. Creatures without any previous fear condition become shaken, shaken creatures become frightened, frightened creatures become panicked and panicked creatures become cowering, unless they succeed at a DC 14 Will save. Cowering creatures are unaffected. This is a sonic mind-affecting fear effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Partial Incorporeality (Ex)

Corporeal spells and effects that do not cause damage have a 100% chance of affecting the ectoshade, not the 50% common to incorporeal creatures. When hit by spells and magic weapons, it takes full damage instead of half. Nonmagical melee attacks can damage an ectoshade, although they deal only half of normal damage and have a 50% miss chance. Ranged attacks are unaffected by this weakness, and ectoshades count as fully incorporeal against ranged attacks.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary, pair, haunting (3–7), or swarm (8–15)
Treasure incidental

Ectoshades are, in contrast to most undead, not created from single bodies or souls twisted by dark magic. They form mostly from scraps left by the souls as they left the bodies. Those beings often manifest in places where many have passed or were laid to rest and a suitable source of energy exists. It often takes a long time, as even a large number of souls leave only minuscule fragments of themselves and it takes a great deal of time for them to meld, twist and condense into ectoplasm. As for the source of energy, those differ from place to place, although most often it’s either a stagnant ley line heavy with emotional imprint (abandoned cemeteries where many grieved or forgotten, brutal battlefields) or residual necromantic energy (near a powerful necromancer’s lair or in a place where undead animate spontaneously). While not exactly mindless, ectoshades are very single minded and simple. They spend their time exclusively wandering, looking for living creatures to unload their hatred upon, but rarely straying from the place where they first came to be. While a lonely ectoshade is hardly dangerous for a well-prepared adventurer, the story is entirely different in the case of multiple creatures. When the point of their creation is particularly abundant in soul residue and energy and left undisturbed for a long period of time, ectoshades can form terrifying swarms, as they are always drawn to their kin. Such a horde can relentlessly pound opponents with their screams, quickly shattering their resolve and falling upon the running or cowering victims with their ghost-like touch, tearing life from them in a quick, piranha-like fashion. Such victims are never left unconscious or tortured, ectoshades don’t pursue such goals. They kill, making sure the victim really is dead and then immediately move on to wander in search of more life to snuff out.

Ectoshades can speak, though almost never do. They don’t negotiate and don’t keep treasures. As amalgamations of soul residue, they don’t have personalities or interests. They rarely serve other creatures unless bent by powerful magic, but don’t mind any other undead in their territories and a cunning necromancer magically disguising himself as one could easily settle in a place overrun by ectoshades as a great means of free protection. Caution is extremely important in such attempts, however, as ectoshades will waste no time murdering the pretender if his mask slips. While mostly incorporeal, the ectoplasm of which they are composed is partly corporeal, even if there’s rarely more than a pound of it in a single ectoshade. This is their greatest weakness compared to more powerful incorporeal beings, as they can be damaged even with non-magical weapons and are much easier to destroy with enchanted arms and spells. Even so, barely visible and thin strings of ectoplasm are all but unhittable at range, so the brave warrior who wants to defeat such a being still has to close in and take his chances in melee, where their touch and mind-rending screams pose an actual danger.
